rst31-v2-hyg-q001.stem: The delivered ingredients look normal, so someone says supplier hygiene need not be checked. Which judgment is appropriate?
options: Check hygiene at the supplier separately from controls in the shop
Assume hygiene is unchanged if the price is unchanged
Do not check the supplier if the ingredients will be heated
If appearance is good, supplier information is unnecessary
rst31-v2-hyg-q001.objective: Check supplier hygiene separately from controls after receipt.
rst31-v2-hyg-q001.explanation: Hazards may arise before delivery. Appearance at receipt does not establish how hygiene was managed at the supplier.
reasons: Controls before and after delivery are distinguished
Price does not verify hygiene management
Planned heating does not replace checking the supplier
Appearance alone cannot verify upstream hygiene

rst31-v2-hyg-q002.stem: Unneeded items are cleared from a passage, tools returned to fixed places and dirt removed. Which explanation of 5S is appropriate?
options: If foreign objects decrease, falls need not be considered
It helps prevent food poisoning, foreign objects and workplace accidents
It only improves appearance and has no relation to food hygiene
After one tidy-up, maintenance is unnecessary
rst31-v2-hyg-q002.objective: Connect 5S with preventing food poisoning, foreign objects and workplace accidents.
rst31-v2-hyg-q002.explanation: Maintaining a clean workplace through 5S supports both food hygiene and work safety.
reasons: Orderly passages and floors also help prevent accidents
The answer includes hygiene, foreign objects and work safety
Removing dirt also concerns food hygiene
The improved condition must be maintained and made habitual

rst31-v2-hyg-q003.stem: A shop manages raw vegetable salad, food served immediately after cooking, and food cooled then reheated after cooking. Which process description is appropriate?
options: Classify food served after grilling as unheated
Treat all three as the same temperature path
Distinguish cold holding, temperature rise, and cooling plus reheating to identify control points
Omit the steps before reheating for cooled food
rst31-v2-hyg-q003.objective: Distinguish temperature paths for unheated, heated, and cooled-and-reheated food.
rst31-v2-hyg-q003.explanation: Temperature changes depend on the actual process. Identify the relevant control points rather than grouping foods by name alone.
reasons: Their different processes cannot be one path
The answer distinguishes the three paths and their control points
Cooling and reheating both require control

rst31-v2-hyg-q004.stem: One process is marked unsatisfactory for a particular day in the record. How should the record be checked?
options: Ignore notes if a checker is entered
Identify that day, process and food, and read the matching notes and checker
Apply the same judgment to every entry regardless of day or food
Read only the food name, not the daily judgments
rst31-v2-hyg-q004.objective: Match food, date, judgment, notes and checker in the critical-control record.
rst31-v2-hyg-q004.explanation: The table links processes and foods to daily judgments. Read notes and checker together to identify which entry was checked.
reasons: Notes still need to be checked even when a checker is entered
The relationships among process, food, date and supporting information are checked
Do not extend a judgment to other days or processes
The food name alone does not show that day’s result
